category_specific_evidence: Reproducer: np.array(['3.14159265358979323846264338327950288'], dtype=QuadPrecDType()); str(a[0]) gives correct 34-digit value.
With np.set_printoptions(precision=34, floatmode='fixed'), repr(a) shows 3.1415926535897931159979634685441852, where digits after ~16 are float64 artifacts.

Root cause per issue: dragon4.c Dragon4_Positional/Dragon4_Scientific only recognize built-in scalar types; PyFloat_AsDouble casts quad value to float64, losing precision beyond ~16 significant digits.
With precision > 16 Dragon4 extends the float64 binary representation producing incorrect digits.
floatmode='unique' with default settings shows only 16 digits (3.141592653589793) instead of 34.
Fix in PR restricts Dragon4 to float16, float32, float64, longdouble and falls back to scalar str formatting for other floating dtypes.
Review comment: a general custom dtype may subclass other top-level types (complex, string); bf16/fp8 and packed types may not be handled by Dragon4.
reproduction_risks: Requires numpy_quaddtype package installed; the regression test skips otherwise.
Printing options are global (np.set_printoptions) and must be reset (precision=8, floatmode='maxprec') after the reproduction.
Exact digits of the float64 artifact may vary by platform, as the test notes.
Default repr of array with QuadPrecDType shows verbose 'QuadPrecision(...)' formatting in some patched versions, which is a separate verbosity issue.
